This Petition Is Coming On For Preliminary Hearing In
'B' Group This Day, The Court Made The Following:
 Order

Captioned writ petition is filed by the owner of offending vehicle against whom the claim petition is filed under Section 164 of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 in M.V.C.No.564/2021 (hereafter referred to as 'the Act' for brevity).

2. The present petitioner/owner of the offending vehicle filed an impleading application seeking leave of the Court to direct petitioner to implead the owner and insurer of the two trailers attached to the offending tractor bearing K.A-49/2229.

The Tribunal, without issuing notice to the proposed respondents, has rejected the application on the ground that claim is made u/sec.164 of the Act and therefore, the owner and insurer of trailers attached to the tractor, are not necessary parties.
Heard learned counsel for petitioner and learned counsel appearing for respondents/claimants.
Perused the order under challenge.

4. Section 164 of the Act clearly contemplates that owner of the offending vehicle or authorized insurer are liable to pay compensation in case of death or grievous hurt due to accident arising out of use of motor vehicle and a fixed compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- can be awarded in the case of death.
The charge-sheet clearly reveals that the two trailers were attached to the offending tractor.
If this factual matrix is accepted, then the owner and insurer of the trailers attached to the tractor are also necessary parties.
A claim petition filed u/Sec.164 of the Act, can be maintained against the owner or authorized insurer of the motor vehicle, which has caused an accident.
The trailers of the offending tractor cannot be isolated and therefore, the findings recorded by the Tribunal being erroneous, a warrants interference at the hands of this Court.

3 NC: 2024:KHC-D:7897 5.
This Court has also noticed that there is a procedural error in the manner, in which order is passed on I.A.No.II.
Without issuing notice to the proposed respondents, the Tribunal has proceeded to pass an order on I.A.No.II filed u/o I Rule 10 of The Code of Civil Procedure.
It is also made clear that 1st respondent cannot insist to array the legal heirs of deceased as proposed respondents, since they have filed a claim petition u/Sec.164 of the Act.
6. The only question that needs consideration under I.A.No.II is as to whether the owner and authorized insurer of the trailers attached to the offending tractor, are necessary parties.

With these observations, this Court passes the following:
ORDER i) Writ petition is allowed.
ii) Impugned order dated 14.07.2023 passed by VIII Additional District Judge and IX NC: 2024:KHC-D:7897 Addl. MACT, Belagavi on I.A.No.II in M.V.C.No.564/2021 is hereby set-aside.
iii) Tribunal is hereby directed to issue notice to the proposed respondents and after hearing the proposed respondents, bearing in mind the provisions of Section 164 of the Act, shall pass appropriate orders in accordance with law.
